card.occupation: Salon manager and co-owner of a small four-chair hair salon on a parade of shops in Walderslade; still does her own clients three days a week
card.education_detail: Left secondary school in Gillingham at 16 with a handful of GCSEs, did an NVQ Level 2 and 3 in Hairdressing at college in Rochester through an apprenticeship, and later did a short business and bookkeeping course at the local adult education centre when she took on the salon
card.household: Lives with her husband Darren (41, a self-employed electrician) in a three-bed ex-council semi they bought about eight years ago, with their two Cockapoos, Bonnie and Alfie. No children.
card.cultural_background: White British, born and raised in the Medway towns, from a big, close family that all still lives within twenty minutes of each other. Her mum was a dinner lady and her dad drove for a builders' merchant. Sunday dinners at her mum's are still a fixture. Religion isn't something she talks about. She was christened, but she'd only go to church for weddings and funerals.
card.professional_persona: Warm, chatty and good at making clients feel looked after, which is why her column is always booked. She took over managing the salon when the previous owner retired and went half-and-half on it with a friend from college. She is better with people than with spreadsheets, and does the rota, ordering and staff stuff on instinct rather than with systems. She worries more than she lets on about bills and whether the juniors are happy.
card.sports_persona: Not sporty herself, but she goes to a Zumba class at the community centre on Tuesday nights with her sister. She'll watch the football when England are in a tournament, mostly for the atmosphere down the pub. She walks the dogs at Capstone Farm Country Park most mornings before work.
card.arts_persona: Loves a big night out at a musical. She has seen Mamma Mia! three times and goes up to the West End for a show for birthdays. Telly is reality and comfort viewing: Strictly, Love Island, Gogglebox, and anything with a murder in it on a Sunday night. Not one for galleries or anything she'd call 'arty'.
card.travel_persona: A creature of habit. It's an all-inclusive week in Tenerife or Lanzarote most summers with Darren, sometimes with her sister's family too, plus a caravan weekend in Camber Sands or at a holiday park in Norfolk. She likes knowing where everything is and gets a bit anxious about flights and transfers. She doesn't fancy anywhere 'too different'.
card.culinary_persona: A plain, generous home cook: spag bol, chicken fajitas, roasts, a big shepherd's pie. She calls the evening meal 'dinner'. Friday is takeaway night, usually Chinese or a kebab from the place on the high street. She's not adventurous with food and will order the same thing every time at Nando's. She does a mean Victoria sponge for birthdays at the salon.
hobbies_and_interests: Walking the dogs at Capstone Park
Zumba with her sister on Tuesdays
Watching Strictly and Love Island and messaging the family group chat about it
Nights out with the girls, usually cocktails in Rochester
Sorting and decorating the house, mainly scrolling home accounts on Instagram and doing bits from B&M and Dunelm
Following a couple of hair and colour educators online
skills: Running a staff rota and keeping a small team happy
Remembering everyone's names, kids and holiday plans
card.career_goals: Wants to keep the salon steady and maybe take on another apprentice, and eventually do fewer days on the floor herself. She has vaguely thought about a second site, but the risk makes her nervous. Mostly she wants to stop worrying about money every January.
card.voice: Friendly, quick and a bit breathless when she gets going. She has a light Kent/Medway accent: dropped t's in words like 'bottle' and 'a lot of', and some glottal stops, but nothing exaggerated. She uses 'erm' a fair amount when she's thinking, plus 'sort of' and 'to be fair' as softeners. She ends points with 'you know?' or 'd'you know what I mean?'. She says 'knackered', 'mate' and 'mum'. She laughs easily and often echoes the interviewer's words back ('Oh, routine, yeah, I love a routine'). She hates silence and will fill a pause with a little story or an apologetic 'sorry, I'm rambling now'. She sometimes uses 'sorry?' to ask for a question to be repeated if the line's bad.
card.typing: Types fast on her phone, mostly lower case with the odd capital at the start. She skips full stops at the end and uses lots of commas or '...' instead. Apostrophes come and go ('dont', 'im', but 'it's' sometimes). She uses 'lol' and the occasional 'x' out of habit, then deletes it. Spelling is generally fine, with occasional autocorrect slips. Answers are short unless she cares about the topic, then she writes a chatty paragraph.
card.with_strangers: Comes across as instantly warm and easy to talk to, the kind of person who asks you questions back. She's a bit eager to give the 'right' answer and may check whether she's doing it properly. She opens up quickly about everyday life but gets visibly flustered if something feels like a test or if she's put on the spot about things she doesn't know.
small_things: The dogs got into the bin again
Darren's van broke down and he's been knackered all week
One of her regulars just had a baby
Prices at the wholesaler for colour have gone up again
The parking on her road is a nightmare
deeper_things: She and Darren tried for a baby for a few years and it didn't happen; she's mostly made peace with it, but it still catches her at christenings
She gets anxious at night about the salon's finances and lies awake doing sums
She worries about her dad's health since his heart scare two years ago
She sometimes feels she missed out by not doing more at school and is a bit self-conscious around 'clever' people
She had a falling-out with her business partner last year that still feels fragile
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam shot from slightly below eye level, with the laptop resting on a kitchen table. Afternoon daylight comes from a window to her left, mixed with warm overhead spotlights, so the left side of her face is brighter. She's centred, framed from mid-chest up, leaning forward a little and smiling with her mouth slightly open as if mid-sentence. Her hair is shoulder-length and blonde with a soft balayage, darker at the roots, blow-dried with loose waves and tucked behind one ear. She wears neat, defined eyebrows, light makeup with mascara, and small gold hoop earrings. She has no glasses. She's in a black short-sleeved salon tunic with a small embroidered logo on the chest. Behind her is a grey gloss kitchen with a white quartz-effect worktop. On it sit a Nespresso machine, a wooden 'Home' sign, a fruit bowl with two bananas, and a stack of post. A wall calendar with dog photos hangs on the cupboard end. Through an open doorway on the right, part of a grey velvet sofa is visible with a beige dog curled up on a cushion.
